functional_requirements.text: All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY handshake. Source generates VALID; destination generates READY. Transfer occurs only when both VALID and READY are HIGH at a rising edge of ACLK.
A source must not wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. Once VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs.
A destination is permitted to wait for VALID to be asserted before asserting READY. If READY is asserted, it is permitted to deassert READY before VALID is asserted.
On master and slave interfaces, there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals.
Each AXI interface has a single clock signal ACLK. All input signals are sampled on the rising edge of ACLK; all output signal changes can only occur after the rising edge of ACLK.
Reset signal ARESETn is active-LOW. Reset can be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion must be synchronous to ACLK.
During reset, master must drive ARVALID, AWVALID, WVALID LOW. Slave must drive RVALID and BVALID LOW. Earliest point a master may begin driving xVALID HIGH is the ACLK edge after ARESETn is HIGH.
Channel handshake dependency rule (anti-deadlock): The VALID of a sending interface must not be dependent on the READY of the receiving interface.
functional_requirements.source: A3.3.1 Dependencies between channel handshake signals

functional_requirements.text: Read dependency: slave must wait for both ARVALID and ARREADY to be asserted before asserting RVALID.
AXI3 write dependency: slave must wait for WVALID, WREADY, and WLAST before asserting BVALID.
AXI4/AXI5 additional write dependency: slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY all asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST before BVALID.
A write response must always follow the last write transfer in a write transaction.
Read data must always follow the read address of the data.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.
For wrapping bursts, the burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16; start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer.
Early termination of bursts is not supported. To reduce data transferred in a write burst, the master may deassert all write strobes but must complete all transfers.
The master must assert WLAST while it is driving the final write transfer in the burst.
The slave must assert RLAST when it is driving the final read transfer in the burst.
When WVALID is LOW, the write strobes can take any value; spec recommends they are either driven LOW or held at their previous value.
Protocol requires that the required number of data transfers must be performed even if an error is reported. The remainder of the burst is not cancelled if the slave gives a single error response.
functional_requirements.source: A3.4.5 Read and write response structure

functional_requirements.text: For a write transaction, a single response is signaled for the entire burst, not for each data transfer.
In a read transaction, the slave can signal different responses for different transfers in a burst.
There is one write strobe for each 8 bits of the write data bus; WSTRB[n] corresponds to WDATA[(8n)+7:(8n)].
A master must issue write data in the same order that it issues the transaction addresses.
The interleaving of write data with different IDs was permitted in AXI3 but is deprecated in AXI4 and later.
When a master issues a write request, it must be able to provide all write data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
When a master issues a read request, it must be able to accept all read data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
All transactions with a given AXI ID value must remain in order; no restriction on ordering of transactions with different ID values.
The slave must ensure that the RID value of any returned data matches the ARID value of the address it is responding to.

The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between: transactions from different masters; read and write transactions; transactions with different IDs; transactions to different Peripheral regions; transactions to different Memory locations.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other.
Slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID, because BRESP must be signaled only after the last data transfer of a write transaction.

error_response_conditions: Write access attempted to read-only location
Access attempted to a disabled or powered-down function

protocol_overview.wire_count: 5 independent channels, each with VALID/READY pair
protocol_overview.endianness: byte-invariant (supports both little-endian and big-endian byte ordering in the same address space)

evidence.quote: All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY handshake process to transfer address, data, and control information. Transfer occurs only when both the VALID and READY signals are HIGH.

A source is not permitted to wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. When VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs, at a rising clock edge when VALID and READY are both asserted.
The AXI protocol uses a single active-LOW reset signal, ARESETn. The reset signal can be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion can only be synchronous with a rising edge of ACLK.
During reset the following interface requirements apply: A master interface must drive ARVALID, AWVALID, and WVALID LOW. A slave interface must drive RVALID and BVALID LOW.

evidence.spec_section: A3.3.1 Dependencies between channel handshake signals
evidence.quote: The VALID signal of the AXI interface sending information must not be dependent on the READY signal of the AXI interface receiving that information.

evidence.spec_section: A3.3.1 AXI4 and AXI5 write transaction dependencies
evidence.quote: The slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY to be asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary. Early termination of bursts is not supported.

evidence.spec_section: A3.4.5 Read and write response structure
evidence.quote: The protocol specifies that the required number of data transfers must be performed, even if an error is reported.

Examples of slave error conditions are: FIFO or buffer overrun or underrun condition; Unsupported transfer size attempted; Write access attempted to read-only location; Timeout condition in the slave; Access attempted to a disabled or powered-down function.
All transactions with a given AXI ID value must remain ordered, but there is no restriction on the ordering of transactions with different ID values.

The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between: Transactions from different masters; Read and write transactions; Transactions with different IDs; Transactions to different Peripheral regions; Transactions to different Memory locations.
